sources.citation: Di Garbo, Francesca & Annemarie Verkerk. 2022. A typology of northwestern Bantu gender systems. Linguistics 60(4): 1169-1239. doi:10.1515/ling-2020-0217 (open access; HAL hal-03955624).
sources.note: No phonology content for Ukhwejo. Sections 4.1 and 5 (pp. 1190-1191, 1213) summarise the Bibaka Ukhwejo gender system after Thornell 2012: eight agreement patterns (four sg, four pl) with five major and six minor sg/pl pairings; realignment to animacy-based agreement (1/2 animate, class-7 prefix y- for inanimates regardless of number); younger speakers generalise y- to all nouns, pointing to loss of gender; variation reported for possessives, demonstratives and the quantifier 'some'. The words tone/stress/accent never occur in connection with Ukhwejo (only a Nzadi tonal-downstep remark elsewh…

sources.citation: Cheucle, Marion. 2014. Étude comparative des langues makaa-njem (bantu A80): phonologie, morphologie, lexique. Thèse, Université Lumière Lyon 2 (theses.fr record 2014LYO20071).

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul (ed.). 2009. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 16th ed. Entry 'Ukhwejo' (ukh). Dallas: SIL. (Internet Archive copy 2011-12-18.)
sources.note: Nothing. Population 2,000 (1996 SIL), Sangha province south of Nola; dialects Ukhwejo, Bikaka, Piiga, Kamsili (Ngamsile); 'Similar to Koonzime, Mpiemo, Bomwali, Makaa'.

sources.citation: Thornell, Christina. 2009. The Central African language cluster Ukhwejo: geographic localization and linguistic identification. Abstract, paper 2-5-3, WOCAL 6, Cologne, 17-21 Aug 2009 (1 p.).
sources.note: Nothing. The abstract describes locating the villages and comparing the four varieties' Swadesh-list vocabularies by cognate strength (WordSurv 6.0); 'some indications that all varieties are not dialects of the same language but rather distinct languages'. No tone, stress or accent mentioned.

sources.citation: Held Mpiemo (mpie1238) files: Festen 2008 (UND MA, Verbal tone in Mpyemo); Thornell & Nagano-Madsen 2004; Thornell 2003, 2004, 2005; Hammarström et al. 2008 (LREC).
sources.note: a full-text search for stress/accent Ukhwejo/Benkonjo/Bekwil: none mentions Ukhwejo (Thornell 2005 names only Bekwil among A80 neighbours); per the mpie1238 check none states a stress rule for Mpiemo either (Festen 2008 is a two-tone H/L analysis with no stress/accent mention).

sources.citation: Connell, Bruce. 2007. Endangered languages in Central Africa. In M. Brenzinger (ed.), Language Diversity Endangered, 163-178. Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter.
sources.note: Only other Glottolog reference for Ukhwejo; an endangerment overview, almost certainly no phonology, listed for completeness.

sources.citation: Johnston, Harry H. 1919. A Comparative Study of the Bantu and Semi-Bantu Languages, vol. 1. Oxford: Clarendon Press. (Language no. 225 'Kaka of Salo', with nos. 221-225a, Upper Sanga / Lobai; data from Ouzilleau 1911.)
sources.note: Nothing: secondhand vocabulary entries copied from Ouzilleau 1911; no prosodic remark on Kaka of Salo.

sources.citation: Ouzilleau, [François-Marie-Frédéric] (Dr). 1911. Notes sur la langue des Pygmées de la Sanga, suivies de dix vocabulaires. Revue d'ethnographie et de sociologie 2: 75-92. Paris: Leroux. (Vocabulaire V, 'Négrille / Kaka de Salo', printed pp. 86-87; Glottolog ref 82908.)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone for Kaka de Salo: a bare French-Kaka vocabulary (c. 76 forms, no tone marks) with the note 'Ces derniers parlent un dialecte bantu très voisin.. des dialectes des Pumpun, des Ndzimu, des Mbimù, des Bumuali, des Boucondjo, Mpomo, Binga, etc., tous dérivés du Fân.' The article's one prosodic remark ('Johnston ajoute qu'ils parlent avec une intonation singulièrement musicale et que leur prononciation est plutôt staccato') concerns Pygmy speech, quoted from Johnston, not this variety.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid ukhw1241 (JSON) and reference records 107997, 116800, 71195 (.bib).
sources.note: No descriptive reference exists (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology; Glottolog's fullest description is only a wordlist from Thornell 2009). Only Thornell's two 2009 conference papers, Connell 2007 (endangerment overview), Ethnologue, UNESCO Atlas, WOLP.
